owner_fcf_series.definition: reported FCF (OCF incl. dividends-in-operating add-back less net capex) minus SBC minus interest income minus lease principal (treatment B); FY2016-18 pre-IFRS16 so lease principal there is finance leases only

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle judgment: FY2019->FY2025 revenue CAGR 8.0% (fleet 331->356, RASK +37%) tempered to ~3% seat growth + ~2% yield/inflation; 3yr/5yr CAGRs start from COVID troughs and are not usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3yr and 5yr CAGRs start in FY2020/FY2022 COVID trough years and overstate underlying growth 3-5x. Equity CAGR is inflated by the FY2021 GBP1.2bn rights issue (FY19->FY25 equity CAGR is 2.7% despite it). EPS CAGRs are undefined (FY2020-22 losses) and the 2021 share-count doubling breaks per-share comparability pre/post. Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined (FY2022 base ~0); SBC-adjusted FCF is far below reported FCF because reported FCF carries GBP130-141m/yr interest income and the deferred-revenue build.
historical_growth.notes: Mid-cycle anchors used instead of CAGRs: post-IFRS16 EBITDA margin FY19 15.1%, FY23 13.8%, FY24 14.6%, FY25 14.2%; headline PBT per seat FY16-19 GBP4.1-6.2, FY23-25 GBP4.9-6.4; net capex FY18-19 ~16% of revenue (previous fleet cycle), FY23-25 9-10%.

scenario_narratives.base: easyJet's axes are (1) fuel and the geopolitical shock to European leisure demand, (2) whether the A319->A321neo upgauging converts the guided GBP250m of cost efficiencies into margin or into lower fares against Ryanair and Wizz, (3) the GBP7bn+ FY26-28 fleet-renewal capex and how much of it is financed into ownership versus sale-and-leaseback, and (4) easyJet holidays' capital-light growth. Base: FY26 is a trough (EBITDA ~10%, headline PBT ~GBP160-200m after a GBP552m H1 loss and the April fuel spike), FY27-28 recover to 14.5% as fuel partly normalises and half the efficiencies stick, and the business settles at 15.5% EBITDA from FY30, between FY19's 15.1% and management's 16.5% target. Owner FCF is negative through FY28 (~GBP-2.0bn cumulative) because net capex runs at 13.5-19% of revenue, then normalises to ~2.5% of revenue once deliveries drop to the c.17/yr steady state. The terminal cap (13x) binds. Value per share is dominated by net cash plus a modest franchise value; it sits well below the earnings-multiple view because the DCF charges the renewal cycle in full and the terminal state earns roughly its cost of capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: The >GBP1bn PBT target is hit by FY28 and held: fuel back near $700/MT, upgauging savings retained (17% EBITDA), the FY27 loyalty programme and premiumisation lift RASK 2-3% above base, holidays keeps growing double digits, and a higher sale-and-leaseback share plus better asset productivity hold mature net capex at 8.5% of revenue. Owner FCF margin matures near 5% and the market pays 14x for it.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fuel stays elevated and demand soft through FY27; Ryanair's cost advantage turns the upgauging savings into fare cuts; margins settle at 12.5%. Management defers and sale-and-leasebacks ~40% of FY27-28 deliveries, so cash burn is contained but lease cost rises and capacity growth stalls at ~2%. Terminal owner FCF is near zero (floored at the 10x cap) and the equity is worth little more than the residual net cash after the burn. No solvency risk (BBB+/Baa2, GBP4.7bn liquidity, no maturity before March 2028) - this is a value-destruction bear, not a distress bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Two-layer valuation because a recommended cash scheme is live. Layer 1 (corporate_action): deal-completes at the PV of Apollo's 715p offer vs deal-breaks at the standalone DCF, weighted 85/15. Layer 2 (the rest of this file): a standalone owner-FCF DCF with leases charged as operating cost, SBC expensed, interest income stripped against GBP1.4bn ex-lease net cash, and the FY26-28 fleet-renewal capex taken from the company's own fleet plan rather than smoothed away; COVID years excluded from every anchor, mid-cycle = FY16-19 and FY23-25. The standalone method values the cash an owner receives, so a capital-intensive airline earning close to its cost of capital on new aircraft scores far below its earnings multiple; that gap is reported, not hidden, and the standalone value (433p) sits inside the undisturbed pre-bid trading range (345-480p), which is the external check on it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Deal completion: the EU/UK airline ownership-and-control clearance for the 49.9%-capped Apollo structure has already delayed the Scheme Document once; a break resets the stock from ~680p toward the 400-450p standalone/undisturbed range. The deal-weighted value assumes 85% completion; at 70% it is ~605p, at 95% ~667p.
Fuel: every $100/MT moves H2 cost ~GBP35m; the April-2026 spike to ~$1,800/MT is the proximate cause of the FY26 trough and its persistence is the main bear axis.
Fleet capex financing mix: the valuation is very sensitive to how much of the 73 FY27-28 deliveries goes into ownership (capex) versus sale-and-leaseback (lease cost); base assumes ~70% ownership.
Competitive retention of the GBP250m upgauging efficiencies against Ryanair's structurally lower CASK.
Terminal capex intensity: 9.5% of revenue at maturity is a judgment on replacement cost of a 389-aircraft fleet; each 1pt is roughly 35-40p/share.

Balance-sheet vintage: March balance sheet against full-year FY26 flows double-counts ~GBP120-220m of H1 FY26 outflow (15-30p/share, conservative) and carries ~GBP1.1bn of seasonal prepayment float that is treated as permanent operating funding.

Upside risk to the model: the DCF gives no credit for the resale value of the new fleet beyond the cash flows it generates; a buyer or an SLB market valuing new A321neos at cost would see a higher equity value than this owner-FCF basis.

corporate_action.status: LIVE recommended cash offer - the share price is pinned to the deal, not to fundamentals; re-check deal status before reusing any number in this file
corporate_action.type: Recommended all-cash acquisition by scheme of arrangement
corporate_action.acquirer: Apollo Global Management (Bidco). Apollo economic stake capped at 49.9% with an EU management trust so the airline stays majority EU/UK owned and controlled; Haji-Ioannou family (c.15.3%) rolling over / irrevocably supporting; rival bidder Castlelake withdrew before the board recommended Apollo
corporate_action.timetable: Scheme Document publication pushed back (Takeover Panel consent, 2026-08-25) to on/before 2026-10-15 while aviation regulators are consulted on the ownership structure; Court and General Meetings expected week of 2026-11-09; completion targeted end of Q1 2027
corporate_action.probability_rationale: 85%. For: board-recommended, founder family irrevocable (15.3%), financed sponsor, 75% vote very likely with a 5% spread and no higher bidder. Against: the one condition that has already slipped is the EU/UK airline ownership-and-control clearance, which is a bespoke structure (49.9% cap + trust) with no clean precedent at this scale; a second delay or an adverse regulator view is the break path. Merger control (EC/CMA) is not expected to be the obstacle.
corporate_action.deal_breaks_value_basis: probability_weighted.weighted_iv - the standalone three-scenario owner-FCF DCF in this file (bear 25% / base 50% / bull 25%)
corporate_action.undisturbed_price_reference: ~480p Jan-Feb 2026 before the Middle East conflict; 345-400p April-May 2026 after it and before bid interest surfaced; 500-580p June on approach reports; 670p by early July; 667-681p since the 6-Aug offer. The standalone DCF (433p) sits inside the undisturbed range, so a deal break would most likely reset the stock toward ~400-450p.
corporate_action.market_implied_probability_note: At 680p against a ~420p break value, discounting the offer at ~4% (the arb convention) over 0.47 years implies ~92% completion; the market is giving almost no weight to the break.
corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv_formula: P x PV(offer at cost of equity) + (1-P) x standalone weighted IV = 0.85 x 678.8 + 0.15 x 433.19
corporate_action.deal_weighted_entry_formula: P x PV(offer at 15% hurdle) + (1-P) x standalone weighted entry price = 0.85 x 669.5 + 0.15 x 233.37
corporate_action.reading: The actionable value is deal_weighted_iv, not probability_weighted.weighted_iv. At 680p a buyer earns the ~5% spread (~11% annualised) if the scheme completes by Q1 2027 and faces ~-36% to standalone IV (or ~-40% to the undisturbed level) if it breaks; at 85% completion the expected value (642p) is ~6% below the price and the 15%-hurdle entry (604p) is ~11% below it. Not an opportunity for a 15%-hurdle investor; a fair-value merger-arb position at best. The three-scenario DCF stays in the file as the deal-breaks leg and as the fundamental view for whenever the deal is no longer live.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, cash generated from operations note (share-based payments add-back GBP38m; FY2024 GBP30m, FY2023 GBP18m). UK filer; no separate net-share-settlement tax line, so equity_award_taxes = 0. The GBP48m 'purchase of own shares for employee share schemes' in financing is the EBT funding of those awards and is recorded as buyback_cash.
inputs.share_count_basis: 764m = FY2025 weighted-average DILUTED shares (AR note 7: basic 751m, diluted 764m; shares in issue ~758m less EBT holdings plus dilutive awards). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. No non-SBC issuance expected; the FY2021 GBP1.2bn COVID rights issue (540m -> 755m shares) is the structural break that makes pre-FY2022 per-share history non-comparable.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote GBp/share. No dual listing to parity-check; the conversion is definitional, not a market rate, so it cannot go stale.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:38:08Z regular session close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP build: UK 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, 5.5% ERP, levered beta ~1.3 for a European LCC -> cost of equity ~11.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.75% (BBB+/Baa2 EMTN curve) -> ~3.6% after 25% UK tax; weights 72/28 on GBP5.2bn market cap vs GBP2.0bn gross borrowings (leases excluded, treatment B) -> WACC 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, fuel and demand shocks are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (FY2025: GBP226m principal in financing + GBP58m interest in operating = GBP284m, 2.8% of revenue) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and the GBP995m lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. Cash-tax EBIT therefore uses D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 total D&A GBP743m less ROU depreciation GBP376m = GBP367m owned D&A (3.6% of revenue). da_pct_path rises to 6% as the fleet moves from 58% to ~85% owned under the FY26-28 delivery programme. Net debt = borrowings GBP2,017m less cash and other investments GBP3,446m = net cash GBP1,429m at 31 March 2026 (ex-leases; GBP434m including leases, the company's 'adjusted net cash').
inputs.notes: LIVE TAKEOVER: Apollo recommended 715p all-cash scheme (announced 2026-08-06, Scheme Document due by 2026-10-15, completion targeted end Q1 2027). The price (680p) is the deal spread, not a fundamental price. Per dcf-methods, a live scheme is valued deal-completes vs deal-breaks: see the corporate_action block for the probability (85%), PV of the offer and the deal-weighted IV and entry price. Everything below is the STANDALONE three-scenario owner-FCF DCF, which serves as the deal-breaks leg and as the fundamental view. MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon (FY2026-FY2035), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file (GBP WACC, lease treatment B, cyclical risk charged once). Fresh build; no memory entry. WHY 10 YEARS: FY26-FY28 carry a fleet-renewal capex supercycle (gross capex GBP1.7bn/2.3bn/3.3bn for 17/30/43 deliveries vs ~GBP1.0bn in FY25) and a demand/fuel shock from the March-2026 Middle East conflict (H1 FY26 headline LBT GBP552m, Q3 PBT GBP85m vs GBP286m); owner FCF is negative through FY28 and only reaches a steady-state margin around FY32-33, so a 5-year horizon would capitalise a trough. FY0 = FY2025 (last reported full year; FY2026 ended 30-Sep-2026 but results are due late November). Year 1 = FY2026E, built from H1 actuals + Q3 trading update + Q4 booked position. VINTAGE CAVEAT: the balance sheet is 31-Mar-2026 (latest filed), half-way through year 1, so H1 FY26's net-cash movement (ex-lease net cash 1,647 -> 1,429, GBP-218m incl. GBP100m dividend) is counted in both the anchor and the FY26 flow: conservative by roughly 15-30p/share. The March cash also carries ~GBP1.1bn of seasonal customer-prepayment float above the September level; the flows only capture growth in that float (wc_capture), the stock is treated as permanent operating funding, which it is while the airline keeps flying. COVID YEARS: FY2020-FY2021 (revenue GBP3.0bn/1.5bn, losses GBP1.1bn/0.9bn, rights issue) are excluded from every anchor; the mid-cycle reference set is FY2016-FY2019 and FY2023-FY2025 (post-IFRS16 EBITDA margin 13.8%-15.1%, headline PBT/seat GBP4.1-6.8). THE FINDING: easyJet converts earnings to owner FCF poorly. FY2016-19 cumulative FCF was ~GBP390m on GBP22bn of revenue; FY2023-25 reported FCF of GBP2.1bn included GBP403m interest income and GBP907m of deferred-revenue build. Through-cycle owner FCF has been ~0-3% of revenue because fleet growth absorbs the cash. The DCF values that stream; an earnings-multiple cross-check (10x FY25 headline EPS 65.3p = ~650p; 10x the >GBP1bn PBT target = ~980p) is far higher, and the gap IS the fleet-renewal capex plus ROIC near WACC on new-build A321neos. The sanity-check multiples will say the same thing from the other side. BEAR FLAG: the bear scenario's terminal FCF is near zero and its interim flows are negative; the value is essentially residual net cash after the renewal burn. That is the finding, not a rounding issue.

bear.rationale: Prolonged Middle East disruption keeps fuel at $900+/MT and European leisure demand soft; Ryanair's cost gap (CASK ex fuel ~40% lower) forces yield-led competition that absorbs the upgauging savings; margins settle at 12.5%, below every mid-cycle year since FY16. Management exercises contractual deferral rights and sale-and-leasebacks on ~40% of FY27-28 deliveries (capex 13% not 16-19%), so lease cost rises rather than falls and growth stalls at ~2% nominal. Terminal owner FCF is near zero: the scenario value is essentially net cash after the renewal burn, which is the finding, not an artefact.
bear.capex_rationale: Deferred/SLB'd deliveries hold FY27-28 net capex at 13%; the fleet stays ~370 with ~30% leased (lease cost 2.7-2.9%), so owned replacement is ~260 aircraft / 25 yrs x ~GBP42m = ~GBP0.44bn plus ~GBP0.3bn maintenance/PDP/IT plus ~GBP0.17bn growth capex at 2% = ~GBP0.9bn on GBP12.3bn FY35 revenue = ~7.5%; 8.0% used. Owned D&A 5% in this smaller, more-leased fleet.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +5%: H1 +12% actual, Q3 +2%, Q4 booked yields flat with load factor -2ppt on +1% seats -> ~+1-2%; sums to ~GBP10.6bn. FY27-28 +6/+5.5%: ASK growth 'up to 5%' from A321neo upgauging (fleet 370->389) plus RASK recovery from the FY26 trough (Q1'27 yields booked up mid-single digits). FY29+ fades to 2.5% nominal (2-3% seats, flat real yield) as the renewal cycle completes.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 10.0%: H1 EBITDA GBP-134m actual, Q3 PBT GBP85m, Q4 ~GBP600-650m headline PBT -> ~GBP160-200m FY26 PBT + ~GBP820m D&A + ~GBP60m net finance -> ~GBP1.05bn. FY27 13.0% and FY28 14.5%: fuel normalises part-way (72-79% hedged at $726-786/MT vs $1,800 April spike), ~GBP150m then GBP100m of the guided GBP250m upgauging efficiencies, loyalty launch FY27. 15.5% from FY30: FY19 15.1% / FY24 14.6% / FY25 14.2% mid-cycle plus roughly half the efficiencies retained after LCC competition (Ryanair, Wizz) passes the rest to fares. Management's >GBP1bn PBT target implies ~16.5%; base does not fully credit it.
base.capex_rationale: Net capex from the May-2026 fleet plan: gross GBP1.7bn/2.3bn/3.3bn FY26-28 for 17/30/43 deliveries, less sale-and-leaseback and disposal proceeds (FY24 GBP114m SLB; guidance frames 75% of deliveries into ownership). Base takes ~GBP1.43bn/1.80bn/2.25bn, i.e. ~30% of FY28 deliveries financed by SLB or deferred under contractual flexibility. FY29 12.5% as deliveries drop toward the c.17/yr steady state (guided GBP1.6bn gross / GBP1.4bn net). Terminal 9.5%: 389 aircraft over a 25-year life = ~15.5 replacements/yr at ~GBP50m = GBP0.8bn, plus ~GBP0.3bn maintenance/PDP/non-aircraft, plus ~2% growth capex on ~0.8x capital intensity, on FY35 revenue ~GBP14.8bn. Owned D&A rises 3.6% -> 6.0% as ownership rises.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax GBP12m on GBP658m statutory PBT in FY25 (GBP8m FY24): brought-forward COVID losses plus UK full expensing (100% first-year allowance, permanent) on owned aircraft. FY27-29 capex of GBP4-5bn into ownership keeps cash tax at zero; ramps from FY30 to 22% by FY35 (25% statutory less the permanent timing benefit of full expensing on a growing fleet). Engine never credits tax on a loss.
base.lease_rationale: FY25 lease cash GBP284m = 2.8% of revenue (principal 226 + interest 58). Falls toward 2.1% as the fleet moves to >75% owned, but not below because ~25-30% of FY27-28 deliveries are assumed sale-and-leaseback.
base.wc_rationale: Unearned revenue GBP1,950m = 19% of revenue at Sep-25; grew GBP907m over FY23-25 on GBP4.3bn revenue growth (21% capture, flattered by post-COVID normalisation). 15% capture on the revenue CHANGE; prepaid model so positive, shrinks automatically as growth fades.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.5% nominal (UK inflation 2-3%, capacity +2-3%, flat real yields). Cap 13x terminal owner FCF, inside the 12-15x cyclical band; Gordon at 9.5%/2.5% is 14.6x so the cap binds.

bull.rationale: Management's medium-term plan delivered: >GBP1bn headline PBT by FY28 (~16.5% EBITDA), full GBP250m efficiency retained, loyalty programme and premiumisation lift RASK, easyJet holidays keeps compounding at low-double-digit customer growth with capital-light GBP250m+ PBT. Fuel back to ~$700/MT by FY27. Higher SLB share and better asset productivity (fewer A319s, 235-seat A321neos) hold net capex at 8.5% at maturity.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): a live geopolitical fuel/demand shock, a 2.5-year capex supercycle whose returns depend on fare discipline in a market where Ryanair sets price, and a bull target that requires fuel, yields and cost retention to all land; no solvency element. Bull 25% (below the 35% default) because it needs three independent things (fuel normalisation, efficiency retention, loyalty/RASK uplift) to go right simultaneously. Base 50%. NOTE: weighted_iv is the STANDALONE (deal-breaks) value. With the Apollo 715p scheme live, the actionable number is corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv; see that block.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
